intro: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev held a meeting in Dublin on the sidelines of the European Political Community summit, while European nations signaled support for Armenia's economic independence. Meanwhile, domestic political tensions persist following the death of an opposition figure in custody.

topics.title: Pashinyan and Aliyev meet in Dublin
topics.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev held a meeting in Dublin on the sidelines of the European Political Community summit. The leaders discussed the peace agenda, including the TRIPP railway project and regional transit prospects. Their aides, Alen Simonyan and Hikmet Hajiyev, also met separately in Dublin.

topics.title: European support for Armenia's economic independence
topics.text: European countries expressed readiness to support Armenia's economic and energy independence during the European Political Community summit in Dublin. Armenia also announced its integration into EU Customs and Fiscalis programs, while the government hailed UK tariff measures as a diplomatic success despite reports they were already in place.

topics.title: Opposition figure dies in custody
topics.text: An opposition candidate died in an Armenian prison amid what opposition sources describe as intensifying political repression. The Institute of Democracy and Human Rights (IODA) and other voices have called for an independent investigation into the death. The government has not yet released detailed findings.

topics.title: Armenia joins Black Sea Trade and Development Bank capital increase
topics.text: Armenia will participate in the capital increase of the Black Sea Trade and Development Bank, subscribing to an additional 7,136 shares. The move aims to strengthen Armenia's engagement with regional financial institutions and support economic development projects.

topics.title: Armenia stripped of CSTO voting rights
topics.text: Armenia has been stripped of its voting rights in the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) alliance. The decision reflects the ongoing deterioration of Armenia's participation in the Moscow-led security bloc amid tensions over the organization's response to Azerbaijani aggression.

topics.title: Armenian chess and boxing achievements
topics.text: Armenian athletes recorded notable successes in international competitions. Vahe Sukiasyan became a two-time European U-18 Chess Champion, while Haik Martirosyan drew with Shakhriyar Mamedyarov in the Total Chess World Championship Tour. Boxer Suren Katvalyan won a bronze medal at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar.

topics.title: Cultural events and publications
topics.text: Several Armenian cultural events took place across the diaspora and in Armenia. Sevan's novel 'The Girl of the Mountains' was celebrated at a book launch in Orange County, while the Yerevan State Pantomime Theatre performed in Moscow. New publications include 'Faithful Saints of Christ' and the Khachaturian International Youth Competition concluded in Beijing.
